lead_in: In Luke 11:41–42 the Law’s tithes meet judgment and charity, which Galatians 5:6 calls faith working through love.

excerpt.text: Doubtless these tithes are your alms; yea even the minutest and most trifling of your fruits do ye tithe; Yet ye leave the weightier matters of the law, judgment and charity. Mark. You have left judgment and charity, and you tithe herbs. This is not to do alms. These, says He, ought ye to do, and not to leave the other undone. Do what? Judgment and charity, justice and mercy; and not to leave the other undone. Do these; but give the preference to the others.
excerpt.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 56 on the New Testament (Ben. 106), §3, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6
